title: Selling a Houston House With a Reverse Mortgage
description: A reverse mortgage does not automatically prevent a house sale. Check the loan type, dated payoff and expected proceeds before choosing a Houston offer.

faq.q: Can I sell a house while it has a reverse mortgage?
faq.a: A sale may be possible, but the reverse mortgage must be addressed. CFPB guidance explains that selling triggers repayment of the borrowed money, interest and fees. Confirm your loan type and the servicer's actual payoff requirements.

faq.q: Is my statement balance enough to calculate what I receive?
faq.a: Use a dated payoff and a complete seller-proceeds estimate. A statement balance alone may not include every amount needed for repayment through the expected closing date.

faq.q: Does an as-is offer guarantee the lender will accept less than the payoff?
faq.a: No. A buyer's proposal is not lender approval or a release. HECM guidance includes conditional rules; ask the servicer and your advisers what applies before relying on a proposed shortfall sale.

faq.q: What if I already received a due-and-payable notice?
faq.a: Contact the servicer promptly and seek appropriate housing or legal advice. Share the notice through a secure channel with the closing team. Do not assume an offer or signed agreement pauses a deadline.
